prompt: Explain how a B-tree index speeds up lookups in a database table.

rubric.referenceAnswer: A B-tree index keeps the key values in a sorted, balanced tree. A lookup walks from the root through a few levels of nodes to the leaf that holds the key, so it takes a logarithmic number of steps instead of scanning every row. Because the keys are sorted, range queries and ordering can use the index too.

answers.text: A B-tree index is a hash table that maps every value to its row. When you search, the database hashes your value and jumps straight to the row in constant time, which is why hash joins are so common. Ranges cannot be searched this way, and the table has to be rebuilt every time you add a row, which is why indexes are always created at night.
